result.title: Neural Interoperability Protocols: Specifying Compatibility Before Training
result.comment: 44 pages. Includes experimental evaluations and appendices
result.summary: Neural networks are increasingly developed as reusable components, yet their intermediate representations remain difficult to exchange across independently trained models. Existing approaches can align representations or encourage compatible features, but successful transfer between particular models does not by itself define what future implementations must satisfy to interoperate. We introduce Neural Interoperability Protocols (NIPs), a specification-first framework that treats neural compatibility as a set of public interface obligations rather than a property inferred solely from model-pair performance. A NIP specifies an exchange boundary, the semantics and admissibility conditions of exchanged packets, and the downstream computations that recipients must support, independently of the architectures and training procedures implementing it. We investigate this distinction through controlled retrieval, vision, and continuous-memory experiments involving independently trained models, differing architectures and objectives, and later training cohorts. Matched-competence controls demonstrate that native task success does not ensure interoperability, while shared semantic supervision enables substantial direct transfer in the evaluated settings. Withheld-information experiments show that recipient models can continue computations requiring information unavailable to donors at exchange time. Partial-contract experiments and packet interventions further establish that observed compatibility is conditional on the semantics, packet populations, and recipient continuations being evaluated. Together, these results support public neural interface specifications as a framework for designing prospective component exchange and distinguishing demonstrated interoperability from stronger conformance claims.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「神经互操作性协议」（NIPs）这一先规范后训练的框架，把跨独立训练模型的中间表示交换定义为公开接口义务：规定交换边界、交换包（packet）的语义与可接受条件，以及接收方必须支持的下游计算；并通过检索、视觉与连续记忆实验，配合能力匹配对照、信息扣留和接口包干预，检验任务成功是否等同于可互操作。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「共享语义监督使中间状态可被独立接收方直接使用」「任务成功不等于状态可交换」的结论，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真正承载可复用视觉内容、以及答案正确性是否代表 latent 内容被使用，提供训练与评测上的核查线索。
